# Environment Variables

How a variable gets from the host into a sandbox process, and which layer owns
which value. Written after telemetry from review-orchestrator sub-agents
arrived unattributed, which took four layers of reading to explain.

Facts below were verified in a live `personal` sandbox (`sb-d4f15c652922`).
File:line references are to this repo unless noted.

## The rule

**`/sandbox/.env` carries what only the host knows. `config/bashrc` carries
how the agent should behave in here.**

Both halves are *inherited*, never sourced by a launcher. That is the whole
lesson of this file: a value that only one launcher establishes is missing for
every other one.

Host knowledge: credentials, the collector's address, which machine this is,
which sandbox this is, which profile it was built with. None of it is
observable from inside the container — `hostname` there is `sandbox-sb-<hash>`
and `$(pwd)` is `/sandbox/source` for every sandbox on every machine.

Container policy: telemetry on or off, which exporters, at what interval, how
much detail. A host's local preference must not silently change it, so nothing
in this category is captured from the host env.

Values derived purely from host knowledge — `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` — are
host knowledge, and are assembled on the host.

## The chain

```
host env  ──ANTHROPIC/CLAUDE/VERTEX/JIRA capture──┐
config/site.env ─────────────────────────────────┤
sandbox.sh literals + assembled OTEL identity ────┴──▶ /sandbox/.env
                                                          │
                          ┌───────────────────────────────┴──────────┐
                          ▼                                          ▼
                   config/bashrc                         bin/claude-wrapper.sh
                   (login shells)                        (interactive launch)
                          │                                          │
                   (container policy)                              │
                          │                                          │
                          └──────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                                             ▼
                                       claude process
                                             │
                                 strips OTEL_* from tool env
                                             ▼
                                    Bash tool subprocess
                                             │
                                             ▼
                             orchestrator (jewzaam-reviews)
                             refills OTEL_* from /sandbox/.env,
                             appends review.* attributes
                                             ▼
                                 nested `claude -p` sub-agent
```

## Stage 1 — host to `/sandbox/.env`

`sandbox.sh` builds `ENV_CONTENT`; `upload_config()` writes it
(`sandbox.sh:786`) and uploads it (`sandbox.sh:794`).

| Source | What | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Host env capture | Only names in `ACTIVE_VARS`, and only if set on the host | `sandbox.sh:1651-1665` |
| `config/site.env` | `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` (from `OTEL_URL`), the Prometheus and Loki URLs | `sandbox.sh:1710-1715` |
| Computed on the host | `SANDBOX_*`, `CLAUDE_DASHBOARD_HOST`, OTLP protocol, `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` | `sandbox.sh:1704-1785` |

`ACTIVE_VARS` is profile-dependent (`sandbox.sh:1651-1656`): `personal`, `home`
and `codex` get `ANTHROPIC_VARS + CLAUDE_VARS`; `work` gets `ALL_VARS`, which
adds Vertex and Jira. Capture is conditional on the host actually exporting the
variable.

**Nothing telemetry-related is captured** (`sandbox.sh:121`). There is no
`OTEL_VARS` list. Exporters, intervals, toggles and log-detail flags are
container policy. The endpoint, protocol and resource attributes are host
knowledge but are written unconditionally further down, which always overrode
capture anyway. `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` specifically must never be captured:
the host's own value names the host's project and session, so every attribute
in it is wrong here.

**No session-identity variable is ever captured.** `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`,
`CLAUDECODE` and `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT` are in none of the `*_VARS` arrays
(`sandbox.sh:92-139`), so nothing that re-sources `/sandbox/.env` can
resurrect a parent session's identity in a child.

### `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`

Assembled at `sandbox.sh:1785` from the `SANDBOX_*` values written just above
it: `project`, `host.name`, `sandbox.source`, `sandbox.openshell_name`, and
`sandbox.profile` when the profile is known.

Two details that are easy to undo by accident:

- **Written single-quoted, not through `printf %q`.** `%q` escapes the
  separating commas as `\,`, and the two consumers disagree about what that
  means: `source` unescapes them, a text parser does not. The review
  orchestrator reads `.env` as text and would ingest literal backslashes.
  Both consumers strip surrounding single quotes.
- **Consumers append to it.** Nothing downstream may assign over it.

No `user.name`: single-user hosts, and the container-side `${USER}` this
replaced was the constant `sandbox` on every sandbox on every machine.

## Stage 2 — `config/bashrc`

Baked into the image, and the only layer every process in the container
inherits from:

- `export PATH="/sandbox/bin:${PATH}"` (line 6)
- **container policy** (lines 18-30): the two telemetry toggles, three exporter
  selections, two intervals, two log-detail flags
- sources `/sandbox/.env` with `set -a` (lines 33-37), *after* the policy, so a
  host-written value still wins
- `alias claude="/sandbox/bin/claude-wrapper.sh"` (line 45)

A login shell reaches this file indirectly: `/sandbox/.profile` sources
`$HOME/.bashrc`. Testing with `bash -lc` and a synthetic `$HOME` that has no
`.profile` will show none of it.

The alias applies **only to interactive bash**. It does not apply to
`subprocess` calls, non-interactive shells, or `dtach`, all of which resolve
`claude` through `$PATH` to `/usr/bin/claude` — which is the point: those
callers get the policy by inheritance, not by resolving to a wrapper.

## Stage 3 — `bin/claude-wrapper.sh`

`connect_sandbox()` execs the wrapper by absolute path (`sandbox.sh:251`). It
re-sources `/sandbox/.env` because a shell that started before a
`sandbox.sh --refresh` holds a stale snapshot, and because it needs
`$SANDBOX_PROFILE` for its own model and codex branching. Then it runs
`validate-profile.sh`.

It sources no telemetry config. There is nothing left to source: the policy is
in `config/bashrc` and the wrapper inherits it like everything else does.
`validate-profile.sh:139` asserts `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY` is set, and
now checks what every process in the container actually has rather than what
the wrapper set for itself two lines earlier.

## Stage 4 — the claude process strips `OTEL_*` from tool env

**Observed, not documented by Anthropic.** A subprocess spawned by a Claude
Code tool call sees no `OTEL_*` variable at all.

Evidence from the verified session, before the identity moved into `.env`:

| Variable | Set by | In a login shell | In a Bash tool subprocess |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SANDBOX_PROFILE` and the other six | `/sandbox/.env` | yes | **yes** |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` | `/sandbox/.env` | yes | **no** |
| `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` | `bin/claude.env` (then) | no | **no** |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY` | `bin/claude.env` (then) | no | **yes** |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA` | `bin/claude.env` (then) | no | **yes** |

The last two rows prove the wrapper chain ran and `claude.env` was sourced —
they existed nowhere else. Every `OTEL_`-prefixed variable from the same two
files is gone while non-`OTEL_` variables from both survive. The strip is by
prefix.

Two consequences shaped the current layout. An `OTEL_*` value cannot reach a
nested `claude` by inheritance at all, so it has to come from a file the
consumer re-reads — `/sandbox/.env`. And a non-`OTEL_*` value survives, so
`CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY` in `bashrc` reaches every descendant.

## Stage 5 — nested `claude -p` (review orchestrator sub-agents)

`jewzaam-reviews/orchestrator/backend.py` builds each sub-agent's env:

- drops every `CLAUDE*` var except the two telemetry toggles, so a nested CLI
  cannot inherit the parent's session identity (`_scrubbed_env`)
- when the inherited env has no `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`, reads
  `/sandbox/.env` and fills in **only** keys matching `OTEL_*` or those two
  toggles (`backend.py:119`) — which is how the endpoint, the protocol and now
  the resource attributes all arrive
- defaults the three exporters to `otlp` when an endpoint is present, never
  overriding (`backend.py:167-170`)
- appends `review.run_id`, `review.stage`, `review.agent`, `review.scoring` to
  `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`, preserving whatever was there
  (`backend.py:257-263`)

A sub-agent therefore reports with the sandbox's full identity plus its own run
correlation, from `.env` alone. No shim, no wrapper.

**What a sub-agent does not get:** `OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL`,
`OTEL_LOGS_EXPORT_INTERVAL` (SDK defaults apply) and `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS` /
`OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS`. They are `OTEL_`-prefixed, so the parent strips them,
and they are container policy, so they are not in `.env` to be re-read. For the
prompt-content flags that is the safer default — they are marked POC-only.
Moving those two into `.env` is the change to make if sub-agent logs ever need
to match session logs.

## Which `claude` runs where

| Caller | Resolves to | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Interactive shell, typed `claude` | `claude-wrapper.sh` | bashrc alias beats `$PATH` |
| `dtach -c $SOCKET claude ...` inside the wrapper | `/usr/bin/claude` | no shell, so no alias |
| `subprocess` from a session tool call | `/usr/bin/claude` | `$PATH` |
| `connect_sandbox()` | `claude-wrapper.sh` | absolute path, `sandbox.sh:251` |

## History

`bin/claude.env` held both halves of the telemetry config and was sourced by
exactly one launcher, `claude-wrapper.sh`. Two bugs followed, and they are the
same bug:

- A bare `claude` — anything not started by the wrapper — inherited an endpoint
  but not `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY`, so it exported nothing. Verified with
  `env -i HOME=/sandbox bash -lc`: endpoint set, every `claude.env` value unset.
- A nested `claude -p` had no `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`, because that was
  assembled in the same unsourced file.

The first fix added `bin/claude`, a `$PATH` shim that re-sourced both files
before exec'ing the real binary. It worked, and it was wrong: a third layer
whose only job was to replay the other two, which also made `claude` resolve
differently depending on whether a shell was interactive.

Deleting it required putting each half where it is inherited rather than
sourced — the identity in `.env`, the policy in `bashrc`. `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`
turned out to be the only value computed inside the sandbox, and every one of
its inputs was already fixed at generate time, so nothing was lost by moving
it. The genuinely dynamic part — a caller appending its own attributes — is
done by the caller.
